hints: Focus on what functional groups fizz with sodium to release a flammable gas, and what that gas must be.
Recall that both -OH in alcohols and -COOH in carboxylic acids release hydrogen with sodium, so check all three compounds for that first test.
Now apply the second filter, the iodoform test needs a CH3CH(OH)- or CH3CO- group, so ask which of the three lack this feature and stay negative.
walkthrough:
**Decode the sodium test**

Think of sodium as a detector for acidic protons. Both alcohols and carboxylic acids react to give hydrogen gas, which burns with a pop.

$$2\text{R-OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{R-ONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Decode the negative iodoform test**

The yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline aqueous iodine is positive only for a specific skeleton. You need $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ in an alcohol or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ in a carbonyl compound.

A negative result means Z does NOT contain that methyl-carbinol or methyl-carbonyl group.

**Test compound 1, ethanoic acid**

It has -COOH, so it reacts with Na to give $\text{H}_2$. It does not give iodoform, carboxylic acids are negative even though they contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$. So 1 fits both clues.

**Test compounds 2 and 3, the alcohols**

Both pentan-3-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, have -OH so they give $\text{H}_2$ with Na.

Neither has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ unit. Pentan-3-ol has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)-}$ and propan-1-ol is a primary $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ alcohol. Both are iodoform negative. So 2 and 3 also fit.

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all possible, the combination is correct.

options.A: Correct. All three contain an O-H group that releases combustible H2 with sodium, and none contains the CH3CH(OH)- or methyl ketone group needed for a positive iodoform test. So 1, 2 and 3 are all possible identities for Z.
options.B: Incorrect. This option leaves out one of the valid compounds. Both alcohols and ethanoic acid pass the sodium test and fail the iodoform test, so there is no reason to exclude any of 1, 2 or 3.
options.C: Incorrect. This option wrongly excludes ethanoic acid. Students sometimes think only alcohols react with sodium, but carboxylic acids react even more vigorously to give H2, and ethanoic acid is iodoform negative.
options.D: Incorrect. This option wrongly includes only one compound. A common trap is thinking pentan-3-ol gives a positive iodoform test because it is a secondary alcohol, but only secondary alcohols with a CH3 attached directly to the C-OH carbon, like propan-2-ol, are positive.
